terms.comment: In Cicero above all a rival candidate for office; Lewis & Short gives it for rivals in general, and Traupman and Morgan–Owens for a competitor in a game or in business. A woman is competītrīx (Cic. Mur. 40).

terms.gloss: a rival, one who tries to equal or outdo another
evidence: Cic. Marc. 1: aemulus atque imitātor (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: As an adjective, emulous, rivalling; in a bad sense, jealous (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: an opponent (in a contest, a game or a lawsuit)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: an opponent in any contest, “in which the contending parties may be the best friends”.

phrases.latin: victōrem forte gymnicī certāminis jactantiōrem cum vīdisset Phryx sophus, interrogāvit an plūs adversārius valuisset ejus.
phrases.english: When the Phrygian sage happened to see the winner of an athletic contest boasting rather much, he asked whether his opponent had been the stronger.
